shortDescription: West African crude differentials held steady on Friday.

children: West African crude differentials held steady on Friday.
Nigerian Qua Iboe offered at dated Brent plus $5.25, according to one trader this week.

There were still some September cargoes of Angolan and Nigerian crude, traders said this week. However, fewer than that total could be available for spot transactions as they could be taken to the lifter's own refineries, the trader added.
In other tenders, Indian Oil Corp has bought 3 million barrels of Middle Eastern crude for delivery between end-September and early October, trade sources said.
"Asian buyers seem comfortable with the number of Arabian Gulf and U.S. crude cargoes headed their way for October and November," analysts at Sparta Commodities said in a note.
"Given the resupply options in October now from Gulf of Oman, (Asian) refineries would be more willing to run up higher even in September as barrels are more likely to arrive than before."
